units.translation: Thus Blomfield and Burges read καὶ τὸν σὸν αὖθις πρόσμολεν [and your brother again came] (thus M, with the accent on the first syllable) ἀδελφεόν [brother]. Hermann connected προσέμολε [he came] with προσέβα [he approached] of Ag. 479.
and your brother again coming, of the same seed

Thus Blomfield and Burges read καὶ τὸν σὸν αὖθις πρόσμολεν [and your brother again came] (thus M, with the accent on the first syllable) ἀδελφεόν [brother]. Hermann connected προσέμολε [he came] with προσέβα [he approached] of Ag. 479.

Thus corrected from προσεῖπε [he addressed] from the annotation of the scholiast: εἶδεν αὐτὸν καὶ ἐφίλησεν [she saw him and loved him], instead of οὐδὲ ἐν μιᾷ ἡλικίᾳ ἔπραξέ τι δίκαιον [nor in any age did he do anything just].
having looked upon your destructive fortunes
nor in the gathering of the beard's hair did Justice look upon him and deem him worthy

Hesychius: πρόσπαιον [sudden] — πρόσφατον [fresh], νέον [new]. The more recent scholiast (Thomas Magister), πρόσφατα [fresh things] · now προσπαίσαντα [having stumbled upon] and προσ-κρούσαντα [having dashed against] them. See Thes. vol. 6 p. 1979.
if sudden evils should not befall

I, unwilling, will fasten you, unwilling, with unbreakable bonds of bronze to this desolate crag
Thus M, unless two correctors corrected the accent to πασσαλευμένος [fastened with pegs].

Προσπορπατός [fastened with a pin], which is in most copies, was invented by a corrector who did not notice that after προσπαρτός [fastened with pegs] ἐγώ [I] had fallen out, which I restored; by which also the other interpolation is refuted, which is in most copies, ἐσίδεσθέ μ᾽ οἵῳ [you see me in what state], for ἐσίδεσθ᾽ οἵῳ [you see in what state]. προσπαρτός [fastened with pegs] is formed from προσπείρω [to fasten with pegs] as σπαρτός [sown] from σπείρω [to sow], χαρτός [delightful] and ἐπίχαρτος [delightful] from χαίρω [to rejoice].
fastened with bonds in the open air

What sound, what scent flew to me, unillumined?

and the lack of money presses upon
Thus Porson for προσπίτνω [I fall before] προσκυνώ [I worship].
